outcome.text: The requested factual outcome was not achieved. The supplied records describe an indoor trial: flowers opened after sunset and closed the next morning, and three of twelve buds opened. They contain no observation identifying a wild pollinator. Establishing one would require direct, documented observations of pollinator visits to this specimen, which are missing.

body.value: Draft an informative exhibit label using current memory and supplied facts. Follow the current scoped word guidance when available. Prioritize a clear, readable first sentence and the large-print species name; move supporting detail off-label. State observations accurately and distinguish observed facts from inference. Do not assert a pollinator or other fact unsupported by observations. Check both fit and factual support before producing the label. Use the executor response_contract. Make no acceptance claims.
Fictional exhibit: night-blooming cactus. Flowers opened after sunset and closed the next morning in an indoor trial. Three of twelve buds opened. No observation establishes a wild pollinator.

For this fictional exhibit, use 35–50 words for the display label; keep supporting details off-label. This replaces the unconfirmed 180–200-word planning assumption. The fictional curator requested the shorter range after approving a 42-word draft (Trial A). Routine visitors usually read the first sentence and large-print species name and skip the provenance appendix. A 190-word label went unread because it did not fit the display (Trial B). A short label also failed when it asserted an unsupported wild pollinator (Trial C), so brevity does not establish accuracy. Treat the range as this curator's guidance, and state only observations supported by the supplied evidence.
